Examples and recipes

Source: vignettes/articles/examples.Rmd
examples.Rmd
library(zumsgpack)

Nanosecond timestamps

A POSIXct is a double, which near 2026 resolves about 2^-22 seconds, so a timestamp’s nanoseconds survive only approximately. When they matter, a handler for type "-1" keeps the fields exactly. The payload is one of three layouts:

timestamp_fields <- function(data) {
  be <- function(b) sum(as.numeric(b) * 256^(rev(seq_along(b)) - 1))
  switch(as.character(length(data)),
    "4"  = c(seconds = be(data), nanoseconds = 0),
    "8"  = {
      hi <- be(data[1:4])
      c(seconds = (hi %% 4) * 2^32 + be(data[5:8]), nanoseconds = hi %/% 4)
    },
    "12" = c(seconds = msgpack_decode(c(as.raw(0xd3), data[5:12])),
             nanoseconds = be(data[1:4])))
}

b <- as.raw(c(0xd7, 0xff, 0xa1, 0xdc, 0xd7, 0xc8, 0x5a, 0x4a, 0xf6, 0xa5))
msgpack_decode(b)                                        # to double precision
#> [1] "2018-01-02 03:04:05 UTC"
msgpack_decode(b, ext_handlers = list("-1" = timestamp_fields))
#>     seconds nanoseconds 
#>  1514862245   678901234

A type of your own

An extension type carries bytes under a number from 0 to 127 that both sides agree on. as_msgpack() writes it; ext_handlers reads it back. Here, UUIDs as type 37:

uuid <- function(hex) structure(as.raw(strtoi(substring(gsub("-", "", hex),
                                seq(1, 31, 2), seq(2, 32, 2)), 16L)), class = "uuid")
format.uuid <- function(x, ...) {
  h <- paste(sprintf("%02x", as.integer(unclass(x))), collapse = "")
  paste(substring(h, c(1, 9, 13, 17, 21), c(8, 12, 16, 20, 32)), collapse = "-")
}
print.uuid <- function(x, ...) cat("<uuid>", format(x), "\n")
as_msgpack.uuid <- function(x, ...) msgpack_ext(37, unclass(x))
registerS3method("as_msgpack", "uuid", as_msgpack.uuid)

id <- uuid("6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8")
b <- msgpack_encode(list(id = id, n = 1L))
msgpack_annotate(b)
#> 0  82                                               fixmap(2)
#> 1  a1                                                 fixstr(1) "n"
#> 2  6e
#> 3  01                                                 fixint 1
#> 4  a2                                                 fixstr(2) "id"
#> 5  69 64
#> 7  d8 25                                              fixext 16 type 37
#> 9  6b a7 b8 10 9d ad 11 d1 80 b4 00 c0 4f d4 30 c8
msgpack_decode(b, ext_handlers = list("37" = function(data) structure(data, class = "uuid")))
#> $n
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $id
#> <uuid> 6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8

A Fluentd forward stream

Fluentd’s forward protocol sends [tag, [[time, record], ...]] messages back to back, with the time as an EventTime extension (type 0: 32-bit seconds, then 32-bit nanoseconds). msgpack_read_seq(each =) reads one message at a time:

event_time <- function(s, ns = 0) {
  be32 <- function(v) as.raw(c(v %/% 2^24, (v %/% 2^16) %% 256, (v %/% 256) %% 256, v %% 256))
  msgpack_ext(0, c(be32(s), be32(ns)))
}
wire <- msgpack_encode_seq(list(
  list("app.access", list(list(event_time(1.7e9, 5e8), list(path = "/", status = 200L)),
                          list(event_time(1.7e9 + 1), list(path = "/x", status = 404L)))),
  list("app.error", list(list(event_time(1.7e9 + 2), list(message = "oops"))))
))

as_time <- function(d) {
  be <- function(b) sum(as.numeric(b) * 256^(3:0))
  as.POSIXct(be(d[1:4]) + be(d[5:8]) / 1e9, origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC")
}
con <- rawConnection(wire)
msgpack_read_seq(con, ext_handlers = list("0" = as_time), each = function(m) {
  for (entry in m[[2]]) {
    what <- if (is.null(entry[[2]]$path)) entry[[2]]$message else entry[[2]]$path
    cat(m[[1]], format(entry[[1]], "%H:%M:%OS1"), what, "\n")
  }
})
#> app.access 22:13:20.5 / 
#> app.access 22:13:21.0 /x 
#> app.error 22:13:22.0 oops
close(con)

Tables

An array of records – one map per row, the way most services send a table – becomes a data frame with data_frame = TRUE. A key a row lacks is NA, and a column of mixed kinds is a list column:

rows <- msgpack_encode(list(
  list(id = 1L, name = "a", score = 1.5),
  list(id = 2L, name = "b"),
  list(id = 3L, score = NULL, tags = c("x", "y"))
))
msgpack_decode(rows, data_frame = TRUE)
#>   id name score tags
#> 1  1    a   1.5 NULL
#> 2  2    b    NA NULL
#> 3  3 <NA>    NA x, y

MessagePack or CBOR

zumsgpack follows zucbor’s design: the same check-then-build decoder, the same limits, the same mapping to R and the same deterministic encoder. A protocol that can speak either changes a prefix:

x <- list(alg = -7L, kid = "11", when = as.POSIXct(0, tz = "UTC"))
str(zucbor::cbor_decode(zucbor::cbor_encode(x)))
str(msgpack_decode(msgpack_encode(x)))
